Business news

  • MSCI Ignites Indonesia Market Reckoning After Months of Warnings — Bloomberg · For the staid and often predictable world of stock-market indexing, it was a bombshell moment.
  • What is a U.S. regulator accusing BMO and TD of doing? Take our business and investing news quiz — The Globe and Mail · Test your recollection of the top stories of the week ending Oct. 16
  • Vietnam Airlines Seeks 25 Airbus Jets to Revive Low Cost Carrier — Bloomberg · Vietnam Airlines JSC is seeking up to 25 Airbus SE single-aisle jets for its re-entry into the low-cost air travel segment as soon as next year, according to people familiar with the matter.
  • China Moves to Restrict Exports of Some Solar Technologies — Bloomberg · China will restrict exports of several solar technologies, as Beijing seeks to maintain its technological edge in renewable energy while countries including the US and India ramp up domestic manufacturing.
  • Bank of Canada’s Tiff Macklem sees energy price challenges for interest rate outlook — The Globe and Mail · Says the longer elevated energy prices go on, the harder it gets to not raise rates
  • China Buys More US Soybeans as Purchasing Spree Gathers Pace — Bloomberg · China has purchased more cargoes of US soybeans, extending a buying spree this week that marks its first acquisitions since the leaders of the two countries held a summit in late September.
  • Canadian home sales forecast downgraded again for 2026 by CREA — The Globe and Mail · Expects sales of 444,530 by year-end, down 5.2% from 2025 and a 1.4% decline from earlier estimates
  • CREA Revises Resale Housing Market Forecast — Financial Post · CREA revises 2026 home sales forecast down 5.2% to 444,530 units, national average price to $681,681, with Ontario and B.C. seeing price drops.
  • Canadian Home Sales Pull Back in September — Financial Post · Canadian home sales fell 2.3% month-over-month in September 2026, down 7.7% from September 2025. National average sale price dropped 1.6% year-over-year.
  • UK Watchdog Proposes Tougher Scrutiny of Microsoft Software — Bloomberg · Microsoft Corp.’s grip on business software is making it harder for customers to switch providers, the UK’s antitrust watchdog said as it proposed tougher oversight of the technology giant.
